subject: Request: one-time credit for SkyForge due to multi-region rollout delay
message_1:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kara Nguyen <kara@skyforge.com>, Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@skyforge.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: one-time credit for SkyForge due to multi-region rollout delay

Hi team,

Quick summary: SkyForge (SF-9821) just informed us their EU launch was delayed by 6 weeks because our multi-region routing for Dedicated wasn't available at the time of cutover. They estimate ~ $120k in lost ARR from the delay and are asking for a one-time credit to bridge them to the delayed capability. Kara is looping in below.

What I'm asking: can product + finance sign off on a concession we can offer quickly? This is time-sensitive — SkyForge has an internal board review on Thursday and wants written goodwill terms.

Details:
- Customer: SkyForge (Enterprise) — expected Dedicated usage for multi-region routing.
- Request: credit equivalent to two months of committed usage (they've proposed ~$60k).
- Root cause: missing multi-region routing automation for Dedicated fleet at cutover (impacts EU region).
- Impact: delayed go-live, lost revenue, risk to onboarding timeline and reference status.

Attachments: deploy_failure_log.txt (customer error snippets), proposal_sketch.pdf (customer ask).

Options I see (quick, pragmatic):
1) One-time monetary credit (amount TBD, needs finance sign-off if > $25k).
2) Structured concession: immediate $25k credit now + contingent credit after engineering verifies fix and customer validation.
3) Non-monetary: extended Dedicated trial in EU + prioritized rollout support.

Why this matters: losing SkyForge as a reference would materially affect our EU GTM for Dedicated. Also we can use this case as a playbook for future multi-region launches.

Can product confirm ETA on the fix and recommended concession? Finance — what approval threshold do we need to route to execs?

Need a decision (or an agreed pathway) by Wednesday EOD to respond before their board on Thursday.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
message_2:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kara Nguyen <kara@skyforge.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: one-time credit for SkyForge due to multi-region rollout delay

Thanks Vivek — digging into this now. Short version: root cause is an orchestration gap for Dedicated when customers requested region pinning + automated failover; we had a manual step in the deployment checklist that wasn't executed for their EU cutover. That is on us.

ETA for a proper automated multi-region routing fix: 3 weeks to ship the orchestration changes, plus 1 week of validation in a staging environment — so roughly 4 weeks to be confident. We can ship a tactical mitigation (route via our edge and partial KV cache warm-up) in ~5 business days to reduce tail latency but it won't be as robust as the final change.

Suggested concession package (my recommendation):
- Immediate: 1 month service credit equivalent to their committed spend (we estimate $30k).
- Short-term: deploy tactical mitigation in 5 business days and guarantee performance SLA for the next 90 days; if we fail to hit agreed latency thresholds after full rollout, remit additional credit up to an agreed cap.
- Long-term: priority seat in the upcoming Dedicated multi-region pilot (no additional charge for 3 months).

Rationale: splits the burden, shows immediate goodwill, ties additional money to verification (reduces moral hazard), and gives customer operational confidence.

If finance/legal are comfortable with the structure, I support this approach.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Prod Mgr, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: one-time credit for SkyForge due to multi-region rollout delay

Laura / team — thanks for looping me in. A few governance notes from finance:

- Approval thresholds: Commercial team can approve credits up to $25k without executive sign-off. Anything above $25k requires VP-level approval and must be documented with the concession reason + customer impact.
- Accounting treatment: a one-time credit will be applied as contra-revenue; we need the exact amount and the effective date to post the journal.
- Risk controls: propose the structured approach Karthik suggested (immediate $25k + contingent up to $35k after verification) so we surface to execs only if necessary. This keeps immediate exposure within delegation.

Attached: credit_workflow.xlsx — shows required approvals and the form Legal needs to execute (we'll need Sign-off by Sales Ops and VP of Finance if we exceed $25k).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm immediate amount we can commit today (I recommend $25k).
2) Draft concession letter that ties any additional credit to verification milestones and performance SLA. I'll own the finance sign-off path and will queue for VP review if we need > $25k.

If you want me to draft the concession letter now, I can—need the technical verification criteria from Karthik and the customer contact for signature fields.

—Marissa
